guard: an expired user bearer is never presented to the broker, and a reconnect that keeps failing is paced instead of repeated at a fixed rate
why: #986 is two independent defects that only together produce the reported storm, so one mutation
cannot audit the fix. N1 restores the dial-with-dead-material half, N2 restores the flat-rate half.
Each names the one cell it must redden; if either survived, half the fix would be untested.
N1 deletes the guard outright, which is the tree exactly as it stood when the issue was filed, so
this is a revert-check and not a contrived edit. Measured on this harness in that state: 11 denials
in 45s, all `"exp" claim timestamp check failed`, all from distinct connection nkeys, gaps
The narrower mutation worth naming here was tried and could not be used: conditioning the guard on
`this.bearerSource` (refuse only where renewal existed and failed) does redden the same cell, but it
narrows the field inside the block and tsc then rejects the message ternary with TS2774. It fails
the BUILD, so the suite never runs and the tool grades it WRONG-RED rather than KILLED. Deleting the
guard covers the same behaviour and compiles.
N2 leaves the guard in place, so no expired token reaches the broker and cell 1 stays green; what
comes back is the flat cadence, which is why its cell is the one that measures GROWTH between
attempts rather than their absence. An attempt-count assertion would have passed here.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. This suite imports @cotal-ai/core by package specifier, which resolves to
dist/, so it audits the last BUILD and not src. Both mutations therefore carry a `command` that
builds core first and an `afterRestore` that rebuilds it — dist/ is gitignored, so restoring the
source alone would leave a tree whose compiled core is still the mutant.

mutations.name: N1 the pre-dial expiry guard is gone, so the endpoint dials with the dead bearer again
mutations.expectRed: an endpoint that cannot renew presents its expired bearer to the broker ZERO times
mutations.cell: an endpoint that cannot renew presents its expired bearer to the broker ZERO times
mutations.note: The pre-fix tree. The renewing arm stays GREEN under this mutation, because a healthy source re-mints before the dial and never had the problem; only the cell watching the endpoint that cannot renew catches this, which is why that arm exists.

mutations.name: N2 the reconnect wait goes back to a fixed interval
mutations.expectRed: the wait between reconnect attempts grows past the flat retry interval
mutations.cell: the wait between reconnect attempts grows past the flat retry interval
mutations.note: A credential that was expired three seconds ago is still expired now. Retrying it on a fixed interval for the life of the process is the load the issue reports; the guard alone moves that load off the broker but leaves the client spinning, so the cadence needs its own cell.
